title: Triple Net Lease (NNN)
name: Triple Net Lease (NNN)
metaTitle: Triple Net Lease (NNN) Property in Los Angeles, CA
metaDescription: What a triple net lease means for a Los Angeles investor, how it differs from other lease structures, and why it is a common 1031 exchange replacement choice.

sections.html: A triple net lease, commonly abbreviated NNN, is a lease structure in which the tenant, rather than the landlord, is responsible for the three major categories of property expense beyond rent: property taxes, building insurance, and maintenance. For a Los Angeles investor exchanging out of a management intensive property such as a multifamily building or a multi tenant retail center, a triple net leased asset can significantly reduce ongoing operational responsibility while still providing direct real property ownership eligible for 1031 exchange treatment.

sections.heading: How NNN Differs From Gross and Modified Gross Leases
sections.html: Under a gross lease, the landlord pays most or all operating expenses out of the collected rent, absorbing the risk of rising taxes, insurance, or maintenance costs. A modified gross lease splits some expenses between landlord and tenant. A triple net lease shifts nearly all of these variable costs to the tenant, leaving the landlord's income comparatively insulated from operating cost inflation, which is a major reason net lease property appeals to investors seeking predictable, lower involvement income.

sections.heading: Tenant Credit Quality Drives Value More Than Almost Anything Else
sections.html: Because the landlord's income depends on the tenant continuing to pay rent and meet its lease obligations, the tenant's creditworthiness is central to evaluating any net lease property. A single tenant net lease building leased to a nationally recognized credit tenant on a long term lease is priced very differently, typically at a lower capitalization rate reflecting lower perceived risk, than a similar building leased to a smaller regional or local tenant without an established credit history. Los Angeles investors evaluating net lease replacement property need to weigh this credit and cap rate tradeoff against their own risk tolerance and income goals.

sections.heading: Lease Term and Renewal Options Matter for Exchange Timing
sections.html: A net lease property's remaining lease term significantly affects both its current value and how it will perform through an eventual future sale. An exchanger acquiring a net lease replacement property with only a few years remaining on the lease term takes on more near term releasing risk than one acquiring a property with a long initial term or multiple renewal option periods already exercised or reasonably likely to be exercised by the tenant.

sections.heading: Common Area Maintenance Reconciliation in Multi Tenant Net Lease Buildings
sections.html: In a multi tenant net lease building, tenants typically pay their pro rata share of common area maintenance costs, and an annual reconciliation process compares estimated payments collected during the year against actual expenses incurred, with any shortfall billed to tenants or any surplus credited back. A Los Angeles investor evaluating a multi tenant net lease acquisition should review the historical reconciliation process to confirm it has been handled accurately and tenants have not been disputing charges, since reconciliation disputes can signal deeper landlord tenant relationship issues.

sections.heading: Rent Escalations Within a Net Lease
sections.html: Most net leases include scheduled rent escalations, whether fixed annual increases, periodic step ups, or increases tied to an index such as the Consumer Price Index, which affect the property's income growth over the lease term independent of market conditions. A Los Angeles exchanger comparing net lease replacement candidates should evaluate the specific escalation structure of each option, since a property with modest but reliable fixed escalations may better match certain income goals than one with market reliant renewal terms.

sections.heading: Lease Guaranty Structures Beyond the Named Tenant
sections.html: Some net leases are guaranteed by a parent company or franchisor even when the named tenant on the lease is a smaller operating subsidiary or franchisee, which can meaningfully strengthen the credit quality behind the lease beyond what the named tenant's own financials would suggest. A Los Angeles investor evaluating a net lease property should determine whether any corporate guaranty exists behind the lease and, if so, review the guarantor's financial strength rather than relying solely on the named tenant entity's standing.

sections.heading: How We Frame the Net Lease Search Within an Exchange Timeline
sections.html: Because well positioned net lease properties with strong tenant credit often move quickly once listed, a Los Angeles exchanger with a defined identification window benefits from beginning the net lease search early and pre-qualifying financing before a specific property is identified, so an attractive candidate can be secured before it is lost to another buyer. We help exchangers structure this search to fit within the forty five day identification and one hundred eighty day closing deadlines that govern the exchange.

sections.heading: Property Specific Review Required Before Any Decision
sections.html:
The general characteristics of triple net lease property described on this page vary considerably from one specific Los Angeles property to the next, and any specific net lease acquisition should be evaluated on its own lease terms, tenant credit, and location by the investor and their legal counsel before a purchase decision is made. Nothing on this page should be read as a recommendation regarding any specific property or tenant.

Buyers new to net lease investing sometimes ask whether a lower capitalization rate on a strong credit tenant property is worth paying relative to a higher cap rate property with a weaker tenant. This tradeoff depends on the investor's priorities: an investor prioritizing income stability and lower risk of vacancy may accept a lower cap rate for stronger credit, while an investor prioritizing yield may accept more tenant risk for a higher current return, and neither choice is inherently correct.

faqs.q: What three expenses does a tenant typically cover under a triple net lease?
faqs.a: Property taxes, building insurance, and maintenance, in addition to base rent, which is why the structure is called triple net.

faqs.q: Does a triple net lease eliminate all landlord responsibility for the property?
faqs.a: No, the landlord retains ownership responsibilities such as structural repairs in many lease forms, lease enforcement, and eventual disposition decisions, even though day to day operating expenses shift to the tenant.

faqs.q: Why does tenant credit quality affect the price of a net lease property so significantly?
faqs.a: Because the landlord's income depends on the tenant continuing to perform under the lease, properties leased to stronger credit tenants are generally priced at lower capitalization rates reflecting lower perceived risk of default.

faqs.q: Does a triple net leased property qualify as replacement property in a 1031 exchange?
faqs.a: Yes, a directly owned triple net leased property is real property held for investment, which qualifies as like kind replacement property under Section 1031.

faqs.q: Why does remaining lease term matter when evaluating a net lease replacement property?
faqs.a: A shorter remaining term carries more near term releasing risk if the tenant does not renew, which affects both current income stability and the property's resale value at the end of a future holding period.
